[/Thinking] To use `\rowcolor` in LaTeX for coloring table rows, follow these steps: --- ### 1. **Load Required Packages** Add these lines to your preamble: ```latex \usepackage{xcolor} % For color definitions \usepackage{colortbl} % For \rowcolor ``` > ⚠️ **Important**: Load `xcolor` **before** `colortbl`. --- ### 2. **Basic Usage** Use `\rowcolor{}` **at the start of a table row**: ```latex \begin{tabular}{cc} \rowcolor{gray!25} A & B \\ % Colors this row C & D \\ \end{tabular} ``` --- ### 3. **Example (Full Working Code)** ```latex \documentclass{article} \usepackage{xcolor} \usepackage{colortbl} \begin{document} \begin{tabular}{|c|c|} \hline \rowcolor{blue!15} Header 1 & Header 2 \\ \hline \rowcolor{gray!10} Cell A & Cell B \\ Cell C & Cell D \\ \hline \end{tabular} \end{document} ``` **Output**: - First row: Light blue (`blue!15`) - Second row: Light gray (`gray!10`) --- ### 🔑 **Key Notes** | Issue | Solution | |-------|----------| | **No color** | Ensure `xcolor` and `colortbl` are loaded. | | **Color name undefined** | Use standard colors (e.g., `red`, `green`) or define custom colors:
`\definecolor{mycolor}{RGB}{200,100,50}` | | **Inconsistent spacing** | Add `\arraystretch`:
`\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.5}` | | **Long tables** | Use `\rowcolors` from `xcolor` instead:
`\rowcolors{1}{white}{gray!10}` | --- ### 🚫 **Common Pitfalls** - **Missing `%` after `\rowcolor`**: ```latex \rowcolor{red} % ← Add % here to avoid extra space A & B \\ ``` - **Using `\rowcolor` outside `tabular`**: Only works inside `tabular`, `array`, or similar environments. --- ### 💡 **Pro Tip** For alternating row colors in long tables: ```latex \usepackage[table]{xcolor} \rowcolors{1}{white}{gray!10} % Odd rows: white; even rows: gray \begin{tabular}{cc} A & B \\ C & D \\ \end{tabular} ``` Let me know if you need help with specific use cases! 😊
